newsitem.title: UK: Physical, paper Brent weaker on fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Physical, paper Brent weaker on fundamentals.

text.p: Physical and paper Brent was weeker on Wednesday, pressured by fundamentals, despite some traders' expectations that North Sea grades would get a short-term boost from lower June programmes.
A Wall Street trader said it bought a May 23-25 cargo of Brent from a British major at June Brent -24 cents or the equivalent of July -16 cents.
This was much weaker than the benchmark crude's earlier talk level, at July Brent +5/+10 cents.
No other physical deals were reported on Wednesday but traders reported two P+C deals on Tuesday for Norwegian grades, Statfjord and Draugen.
They also said an end May Statfjord changed hands at a premium of some 26 cents to Dated Brent late on Monday, in line with the grade's recent levels.
Many North Sea traders said they remained bearish, despite a lower than expected June loading programme for Norwegian sweet grade Oseberg.

But some said they were awaiting the other programmes, namely Brent and Forties which are expected on Thursday, adding that if they were lower than the May programmes also, then the market could get a shot in the arm.

"I still think it is going to come off. The U.S. stock build is bearish and refiners have built up stocks here over the past few weeks. Fundamentally we are not looking good," one North Sea producer said.
Norway's Oseberg production in June will be hit sharply by schuduled field maintenance.
The sweet crude system is due to load the equivalent of 30.7 standard cargoes of 500,000 barrels each in June compared with 44.2 May cargoes, traders said.
